question: Where must regulatory signs be installed, and what nighttime-visibility requirement applies?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Regulatory signs must be installed at or near where the regulations they convey apply, and they must clearly indicate the requirements and be designed and installed for adequate visibility and legibility to obtain compliance. For nighttime visibility, regulatory signs must be either retroreflective or illuminated (per Section 2A.21). Special contexts (preferential lanes, toll plazas, ramp meters) add placement provisions. Standards (mandatory): - "Regulatory signs shall be used to inform road users of selected traffic laws or regulations and to indicate the applicability of the legal requirements." - "Regulatory signs shall be installed at or near where the regulations apply. The signs shall clearly indicate the requirements imposed by the regulations and shall be designed and installed to provide adequate visibility and legibility in order to obtain compliance." - "Regulatory signs shall be retroreflective or illuminated (see Section 2A.21)." - "If used, overhead Preferential Lane (R3-13 series, R3-14 series, and R3-15 series) regulatory signs shall be installed on the side of the roadway where the entrance to the preferential lane is located and any appropriate adjustments shall be made to the sign message." Guidance (recommended): - Regulatory signs (or regulatory panels within guide signs) indicating restrictions on vehicle type and forms of toll payment at a specific toll plaza lane should be installed over the applicable lane, either on the toll plaza canopy or on a separate structure immediately in advance of the canopy, located so each sign is clearly related to an individual toll lane. Options (permitted): - Where ramp control signals are used to meter traffic on a freeway or expressway entrance ramp, regulatory signs with legends appropriate to the control may be installed adjacent to the ramp control signal faces. Visual evidence: [Image 7] shows the full text of Section 2B.01, including the Standard provisions that regulatory signs shall be installed at or near where regulations apply and shall be retroreflective or illuminated. [Image 3] (Table 2A-4) lists means of retroreflection and illumination of sign elements (e.g., prismatic reflector buttons, LEDs, reflective materials), supporting how the retroreflectivity/illumination requirement can be met. [Image 2] (Figure 2A-1) illustrates conspicuity enhancements for signs, including retroreflective strips on sign supports and LEDs in a sign border, which relate to visibility of regulatory signs such as the STOP sign. [Image 4] (Figure 2B-3) shows examples of regulatory Speed Limit signs and plaques that are subject to these installation and visibility requirements. Citations: - Section 2B.01 Standard §1 (p.67) - Section 2B.01 Standard §2 (p.67) - Section 2B.01 Standard §3 (p.67) - Section 2G.03 Standard §10 (p.409) - Section 2F.04 Guidance §3 (p.383) - Section 2B.61 Option §1 (p.135) - Page 108 - Table 2A-4 (p.62) - Figure 2A-1 (p.48) - Figure 2B-3 (p.86)
